sources.title: Mock reference notes, quadratic equations (written for testing the knowledge base)

passages.text: An equation is a statement that two expressions are equal. Putting a value in place of the unknown either makes the statement true or false.
A quadratic equation is an equation that can be written in the form a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero, where a, b and c are real numbers and a is not equal to zero.
A root of a quadratic equation is a value of the unknown that makes the equation true. A quadratic equation has at most two roots. If a root is put back into the equation, both sides are equal.
If the roots of a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero are p and q, then the sum of the roots p plus q equals minus b divided by a, and the product of the roots p times q equals c divided by a.
A common slip is to write the sum of the roots as b divided by a. The sign matters: the sum is minus b divided by a.
